summary: A stop or kill of an exec runtime in its first moments now reaches it. Until the user manager had started an exec's systemd scope, a signal sent to the scope reached nothing, so the exec ran on: `st agents stop` of an exec, a replaced or moved exec, a gate or metric runner over its time limit, and `st3 service reset` or uninstall could each leave a just-started exec running

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Signals to an exec that has joined its scope are unchanged. Before it has joined, its process group, which then holds only systemd-run, gets the signal as well, so the exec ends before its task starts.

downtime.detail: No startup work or expected interruption.

manual.detail: No operator action. An exec left running by the old behaviour can be stopped again with `st agents stop`, or ended with `systemctl --user stop` on its st3-*.scope.

recovery.detail: No persistent state; an older build only reintroduces the lost signal.
